**Can confirm — this migration completely broke all active sessions.**

I'm running opencode `1.15.13` (stable, not `dev`). After the migration ran, every single session that hits the `session_message` write path is now dead. Messages type fine but silently disappear on Enter.

**What I observed:**

| Table | Rows | Status |
|-------|------|--------|
| `session_message` | 0 | Wiped by migration |
| `session_input` | 0 | Wiped by migration |
| `event` | 0 | Wiped by migration |
| `message` | 51,804 | Still intact |
| `part` | 27,231+ | Still intact |

**The breakage cascade:**

1. Migration clears `session_message` (projection) and `event` (source of truth)
2. Next time any session tries to write to `session_message`, the `seq` column computes as `MAX(seq) + 1` → `NULL + 1 = NULL`
3. SQLite rejects with `NOT NULL constraint failed: session_message.seq`
4. Message insert silently fails — typed messages vanish from the UI

**Log evidence** (from `~/.local/share/opencode/log/`):

ERROR NOT NULL constraint failed: session_message.seq
  cause=SQLiteError: NOT NULL constraint failed: session_message.seq
    at appendMessage (/$bunfs/root/chunk-9re0szbd.js:2:62522)
    at session.next.agent.switched (/$bunfs/root/chunk-9re0szbd.js:2:56643)

This happens on **every** message send attempt — not just compacted sessions. Compacted sessions broke first because compaction triggers `appendMessage` via `session.next.agent.switched`, but the same error hits any session once it hits that code path.

**Critical detail:** The `message` and `part` tables still have all the actual conversation data. The event-sourced projections are what's destroyed. But since `DELETE FROM event` removed the source of truth, there's no way to rebuild those projections without a migration fix from the opencode team.

**Environment:** macOS 15.x, opencode 1.15.13, Ghostty terminal, `zai-coding-plan/glm-5.1` provider

@Rakesh-207 — your cascade analysis is exactly right, and it fills in the gap my report left open.

The reason our `session_message` schemas differ: I'm on `dev` (post-#30785), so my schema was already at the new version when the migration ran. No `seq` column, so I didn't hit the NOT NULL failure. I just hit the empty session list from the `workspace_id = NULL` problem.

You're on `1.15.13` stable, where the migration ran against the old schema that still has `seq`. Same migration, two different failure modes depending on which schema version you started from.

So the full picture:

- **Stable users (1.15.13)**: `session_message.seq` becomes NULL → NOT NULL constraint fails → messages silently vanish on every send
- **Dev users**: schema difference avoids the seq failure, but `workspace_id = NULL` on all sessions → `/sessions` shows nothing

Also — I walked back my concern about `DELETE FROM event` in the issue body, but your findings restore it. The `message` and `part` tables being intact means the conversation content isn't gone, but with `event` wiped there's no source of truth to re-project `session_message` from. The projections can't be rebuilt correctly without a follow-up migration from the team.

The `message` table is the V1 store. The `event` table was the V2 event log. This migration cleared the V2 layer entirely but left the V2 projection code in place expecting it. That's the mismatch.

yeah that's fair, the original version was half-doing it which is what made it weird. reworked it so the discard is way more targeted:
- it only runs on empty-stream truncations now (the EmptyOther case), not every retry. rate limits / 5xx etc retry untouched like before, so no behavior change there
- when it does discard, it now removes everything the failed attempt created (via a per-call part floor), not just the text/reasoning. that was the actual bug — we were leaving an orphan step-start behind on each retry, so you'd get duplicate step separators piling up
- also discards on the final give-up (when the 3-retry cap is hit) so a failed message doesn't keep the leftover either

On the ux side: for empty truncations there's no visible content to flicker (0 output tokens, it's basically just the step-start), so nothing the user was reading disappears. the existing "retrying" indicator still shows. i deliberately left the broader "discard partial content on any mid-stream retry" case out of scope since that's where the tool side-effect / flicker concerns actually live.

Confirmed locally: this commit matches the root cause I saw.

With the same Bedrock/Aperture setup and prompt `Reply with OK only`, running OpenCode under `browser` conditions reproduces the empty response: only `step_start`, no text, no stderr. Running the same code under `node` conditions returns `OK`.

So the Smithy decode error I saw appears to be a consequence of the release bundle resolving the browser exports. My earlier Smithy override worked by avoiding that bad browser path; this commit fixes it more directly by building with `conditions: ["node"]`.

I fixed the issue with PR #30979.

**Bug 1** was in `instruction.ts:extract()` — it skipped read parts with `time.compacted` set, but `metadata.loaded` (the list of instruction files already attached) survives compaction unchanged. This caused `resolve()` to re-attach `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`/`CONTEXT.md` on every read after prune.

**Bug 2** was in `compaction.ts:prune()` — `break loop` when encountering an already-compacted part exited the outer message scan, so older prunable tools were silently skipped on all subsequent prune runs.

Both are 1-line fixes. Regression tests added for each.

- **Tests:** workflow/tool suites 7 → 37; all six HTTP endpoints in the httpapi exercise gate; full package suite 3064 pass / 0 fail.

I reproduced this on Windows Desktop and found the old-layout regression root cause:

`isDesktopV2` was converted to `createMemo(...)`, but the JSX gate in `SessionHeader` still uses `when={isDesktopV2}` instead of `when={isDesktopV2()}`.

Because a function reference is always truthy, the legacy fallback branch never renders, which hides the old-layout right-side toolbar buttons (including the open-folder / open-in-file-manager control).

Minimal fix:

```tsx
<Show when={isDesktopV2()} fallback={...}>
```

I verified this locally in a desktop build and it restores the old-layout buttons.

This looks separate from the V2 parity issue tracked in #29875.
